correctness.rationale: All hypotheses and quantifiers are fixed: n=3k+1, k>=2, every labelled minimum maximal matching. The established bracelet graph admits invertible scaling to two separated particles. Three exhaustive cyclic-order cases give the uniform floor(n/2) upper bound. A pair-dependent explicit target has unrestricted circle-assignment lower bound floor(n/2); because every legal move shifts one particle by one circle edge, this is also a legal-path lower bound. Both actual standalone implementations were run and passed, checking each finite configuration and every eccentricity, plus an exhaustive isomorphism to the direct cycle matching graph. Infinite conclusion relies on the proof, not extrapolation.

originality.rationale: 2010 independent-set reconfiguration and 2014 domination reconfiguration introduce related questions, not the cycle metric. The 2022 thesis and March 2023 article give the exact bracelet adjacency and counts; their relevant full-text cycle sections and Hamiltonicity sections were inspected. They do not state or prove the exact common eccentricity formula. The new theorem concerns the non-immediate all-vertex metric of this known family, not a new graph identification. Actual mathematical-record searches and accessible older mathematical claims were compared by implication. Possible alternative terminology remains a residual risk.
residual_risks: The known full bracelet adjacency determines its metric in principle; an earlier derived closed diameter/eccentricity theorem indexed under other terminology may exist.
No independent scholarly audit has been performed.

value.rationale: Shortest replacement paths are the natural quantitative measure of moving among optimal edge-dominating matching configurations. A complete family of nonregular reconfiguration graphs is proved self-centered with a sharp, uniformly attained linear radius/diameter and an explicit farthest target from every state. Counts, degrees, connectivity and Hamiltonicity alone do not supply these metric facts; the result has natural all-parameter scope and is not a purely arbitrary finite statistic.
